Solver artifacts of a stored scenario

Source: R/portability.R
scenario_artifacts.Rd

Lists what each solve left on disk — whether its solution was imported, what the scratch costs, and which rows are safe to clean up. Read-only.

Usage

scenario_artifacts(object)

Arguments

object

a scenario object.

Rows for the scenario-level derived tiers are listed too, distinguished by kind: "reports" for rendered reports and "levcost" for cached levcost results. They sit beside runs/ rather than inside it, and each has its own remover — clear_report_cache() and clear_levcost_cache() — so drop_solver_outputs(), a run cleaner, leaves them alone.

Value

a tibble: kind, run, variant, solve, status, imported, scratch_mb, solution_mb, active, sealed, has_record, path, suggest.

Details

The scratch_mb column counts the regenerable part: the generated model source, the exchange input/, solver logs, and output/ only when the solution has been imported into modOut/. Until that has happened output/ is the only copy of the solution and is never counted as scratch, whatever status says — status == "solved" records that the solution reached memory, not disk.

suggest is a reason string, empty when the row is not a candidate. A sealed scenario suggests nothing. The active run is suggested like any other — unlike drop_scenario_run(), cleaning scratch keeps the record and the solution, so the run stays listed and readable.

See also

drop_solver_outputs(), scenario_runs(), clear_report_cache()

Examples

# \donttest{
ek   <- topia$modules$electricity$R3
mod  <- newModel("TOPIA", data = ek$repo,
                 calendar = topia$modules$calendars$s4_h24,
                 region = ek$regions,
                 horizon = topia$modules$horizons$base,
                 discount = 0.05)
mod <- setGeoscale(mod, ek$geoscale)
scen <- interpolate_model(mod, name = "EX")
#> Cost declared at a coarse geoscale level:
#>   TBD_COA_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#>   TBD_GAS_WEST_CENTRAL@invcost: CENTRAL, WEST
#> The cost is charged ONCE at that cell rather than at each child region, and is discounted at the children's rate. That is usually what a national cost datum means -- said here because it is a different number from naming the children individually.

# what exists on disk for this scenario, and what could be dropped
scenario_artifacts(scen)
#> # A tibble: 0 × 13
#> # ℹ 13 variables: kind <chr>, run <chr>, variant <chr>, solve <chr>,
#> #   status <chr>, imported <lgl>, scratch_mb <dbl>, solution_mb <dbl>,
#> #   active <lgl>, sealed <lgl>, has_record <lgl>, path <chr>, suggest <chr>
# }
